editorial:
Imagine being a serious lawyer and having to defend a guy whose only witness is a ghost from the 1600s. That is exactly the mess Emi finds herself in. You get to watch her go from being totally skeptical to actually talking to Rokubei, a spirit who has been hanging around for over four hundred years. The movie feels like a quirky stage play brought to life, mixing courtroom drama with some really silly supernatural moments. It is a lighthearted ride that does not take itself too seriously, making it a great choice for a lazy weekend afternoon.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between the characters and the funny way the court case unfolds. The pacing stays snappy, though some of the side plots might feel a bit slow if you are looking for a fast thriller. If you enjoy seeing a grumpy prosecutor get outsmarted by a ghost, you will love this. You should definitely try to find it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the great costume details, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch. It is a charming flick that balances laughs and mystery perfectly.
endingExplained: In the end, the trial reaches a wild peak when the ghost's testimony actually helps prove the husband is innocent. You find out the real killer was someone else entirely who tried to frame him. Once the truth comes out and the legal battle is over, Rokubei finally finds peace. He gets to move on to the afterlife, leaving Emi with a new perspective on life and death after their strange friendship.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky legal dramas and ghostly comedies.
